entities.name: Because AA stacking vertically aligns Sb atoms, it increases Sb-pz orbital overlap, causing strong interlayer repulsion and a larger interlayer separation; by c
entities.description: Because AA stacking vertically aligns Sb atoms, it increases Sb-pz orbital overlap, causing strong interlayer repulsion and a larger interlayer separation; by contrast, lateral displacement in AB reduces overlap and repulsion, yielding a smaller interlayer separation.
entities.evidence_span: In the AA stacking, the vertical alignment of Sb atoms leads to significant overlap of the out-of-plane Sb–pz orbitals [as shown in Figure 1(d)], resulting in strong interlayer re- pulsion and, consequently, a large interlayer separation of approximately 3.7 ˚A.

evidence_spans: In the AA stacking, the vertical alignment of Sb atoms leads to significant overlap of the out-of-plane Sb–pz orbitals [as shown in Figure 1(d)], resulting in strong interlayer re- pulsion and, consequently, a large interlayer separation of approximately 3.7 ˚A.

In contrast, the AB stacking, where Sb atoms are laterally displaced, minimizes orbital over- lap, reducing interlayer repulsion and yielding a smaller separation of about 2.1 ˚A ; see Supplementary Fig. 1(b) for details.

entities.evidence_span: As shown in Figures. 2(b) and 2(e), the optimized structures exhibit a continuous modulation of the interlayer separation d, which directly determines the local topological character, as reflected in the Z2 phase diagrams [Figs. 2(c) and 2(f)].

evidence_spans: Across an isolated M = 0 contour, a single chiral Dirac mode appears in a single time-reversal fixed sector, while its partner adds the counter-propagating mode in the second sector.
